clue.text: Summary established after excavation

indicators.note: after places the word for established behind the word for excavation

parts.note: an excavation is a dig
EST is the abbreviation for established, as on shop signs giving a founding year

explanation.surface: A report sums up what was found once the archaeologists finished digging.
explanation.definitionFit: A synopsis or condensed account is a digest, as in a digest of the week's news.

clue.text: Birth that might take 3-5 days

definitions.meaning: a birth is the ... of a baby
a parcel's posting is promised within so many working days

explanation.surface: A long labour ward wait, apparently lasting several days.
explanation.definitionFit: Childbirth and the shipping of a parcel are both senses of the same noun for handing over.

clue.text: Craving? Regularly gorge on ends of rye bread

indicators.note: regularly means take every other letter of gorge, starting with the first
ends of means the final letter of each of the words rye and bread

explanation.surface: Someone with a craving stuffs themselves on rye bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Greed is an excessive craving for food or wealth; the question mark nods to gluttony in the surface.

clue.text: So horse, reportedly, that is right, gets wetter

indicators.note: reportedly means we write letters that sound like the spoken word for a horse

parts.note: a gee-gee is a childish word for a horse
i.e. is the abbreviation for that is (id est)

explanation.surface: A horse, people say, is drenched and getting wetter.
explanation.walkthrough: GEE-GEE is pronounced like the letters G G, so 'reportedly' gives GG.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of soggy: more soaked or sodden with water.

clue.text: Good person, simple on reflection, loses temper?

indicators.note: on reflection means the combined letters are seen as in a mirror, back to front

parts.note: a saint, abbreviated ST, is a good person
simple can mean pure, unmixed

explanation.surface: A placid soul, thinking things over, finally snaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' turns STPURE round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a person explodes with anger as a volcano does, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Engineer Joe and me succeeded, creating rules

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, the British Army's engineering corps
GI Joe is a nickname for an American soldier, so Joe gives GI
S is the usual abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: An engineer called Joe and I did well and drew up the regulations.
explanation.definitionFit: Governments or systems of administration are regimes, ways of ruling a country.

clue.text: Description of friend holding gold plate

indicators.note: holding means the word for friend wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: a pal is a friend
OR is the heraldic word for gold
a tray is a flat dish, a plate

explanation.surface: An account of a mate carrying a golden dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A depiction or rendering of something in words or pictures is a portrayal.

clue.text: Seat is prepared for rest of the afternoon?

indicators.note: prepared means the letters of seat is are made ready in a new order

explanation.surface: A chair has been set up for a lazy afternoon.
explanation.definitionFit: A nap taken after lunch in hot countries; the definition is playful, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Irritant that could make everyone strangely green

parts.note: everyone means all

indicators.note: strangely means the letters of green are jumbled

explanation.surface: Something that might turn everybody an odd shade of green.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance provoking an immune reaction, such as pollen, is an irritant to sufferers.

clue.text: Fools new in company, politician has surprised expression

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician
oops is an exclamation of surprise at a mistake

explanation.surface: Idiots joining a firm leave an MP looking startled.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly or foolish people are nincompoops, a jocular word for idiots.

clue.text: Ranged around park

indicators.note: around means the letters of ranged are turned about into another order

explanation.surface: Something spread out round a public park.
explanation.definitionFit: A park is a public garden or landscaped grounds, so the words overlap in sense.

clue.text: Eager to behead Welsh saint?

indicators.note: to behead means remove the first letter of the saint's name

parts.note: St David is the patron saint of Wales

explanation.surface: Someone keen to decapitate a holy man of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen and enthusiastic, as an avid reader is.

clue.text: Not the calculating type, instinctive about hesitation — and another?

indicators.note: about means the word for instinctive goes round the hesitations

parts.note: innate means instinctive, inborn
um is a sound of hesitation
another hesitation, er

explanation.surface: Someone who isn't scheming, going by gut feel and hesitating again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: Unable to do arithmetic; the definition plays on 'calculating' meaning scheming as well as counting.

clue.text: Unpredictably but properly entertaining start to rowboat race at sea

indicators.note: entertaining means the adverb for properly holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: piously means dutifully, properly in a religious sense

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of rowboat
at sea means the letters of race are in confusion

explanation.surface: A rowing race at sea run with unpredictable decorum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Properly' here means in a devout, dutiful way, which is why it can stand for PIOUSLY; 'at sea' gives ECAR, and 'entertaining' takes R plus those letters in.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in an unstable, insecure way that could go wrong at any moment.

clue.text: Fish break into chippy

parts.note: a carp is a freshwater fish
to enter is to break into a building

explanation.surface: A fish breaks into a fish-and-chip shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chippy' is British slang both for a fish-and-chip shop and for a carpenter; here it means the latter.
explanation.definitionFit: Chippy is informal British slang for a woodworker, from the chips of wood.

clue.text: The least dodgy sportspeople?

indicators.note: dodgy means the letters of the least are unreliable and get reordered

explanation.surface: The most honest competitors, or the ones who dodge least?
explanation.definitionFit: Track and field competitors are a kind of sportspeople.

clue.text: Go over and back down again?

parts.note: the prefix re- means again
to capitulate is to back down, surrender

explanation.surface: Revisit, then retreat and give in once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To summarise or repeat the main points is to go over them again.

clue.text: Exchanges around whiskey and nuts

indicators.note: around means the word for exchanges goes about the letter for whiskey

parts.note: to cash a cheque is to exchange it for money
Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A bar swaps whiskey for bar snacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Kidney-shaped edible seeds from a tropical tree, sold as nuts.

clue.text: Samples guinea pigs

definitions.meaning: small trial pieces of perfume or paint are samples
people on whom a product is tried out are guinea pigs

explanation.surface: A lab tries things out on guinea pigs.
explanation.definitionFit: Both trial specimens and people trying products are given the same plural noun.

clue.text: Complain — the thing is …?

definitions.meaning: to protest or raise an objection
a thing, an item or article

explanation.surface: Someone protests, then trails off about what the thing is.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb sense: to protest; noun sense: a physical item or article.

clue.text: Things given by old boy before booze-ups

indicators.note: before means the old boy's letters come ahead of the drinking bouts

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a session is a long drinking bout

explanation.surface: A former pupil gives presents ahead of heavy drinking nights.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a thing about something means a fixation, so fixations are things.

clue.text: Lone duck seen chasing Spanish sun

indicators.note: chasing means the duck follows behind the sun

parts.note: sol is Spanish for sun
a duck is a zero score in cricket, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A single duck is spotted following the Spanish sunshine.
explanation.definitionFit: Done alone, single-handed, as in a flight made by one pilot.

clue.text: Stuffed, some diners ate dinner

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few diners finished their meal full up.
explanation.definitionFit: Full to satisfaction after eating, having had one's fill.

clue.text: Solve or create first of two clues occasionally

parts.note: to set a puzzle is to create it

indicators.note: first of means the initial letter of two
occasionally means take only some letters of clues, the second and fourth

explanation.surface: A setter is asked to crack or compose a couple of clues now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle a dispute or question is to resolve it.

clue.text: Observe detailed piece by art gallery

indicators.note: detailed means de-tailed: the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a speck is a tiny piece
the Tate is a group of British art galleries in London and elsewhere

explanation.surface: An intricate artwork displayed beside a gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' is read as de-tailed, removing K from SPECK to give SPEC.
explanation.definitionFit: To watch an event as an onlooker, as a spectator does.

clue.text: Violently hurt by quiet bird

indicators.note: violently means the letters of hurt are thrown about

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone badly injured by a silent bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A songbird such as the song thrush or mistle thrush.

clue.text: Main songs? They're not heard by everybody

definitions.meaning: the lead tracks on singles were on the A side of the record
remarks made to the audience or in an undertone, not for all ears

explanation.surface: Principal tunes that only some people get to hear.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatrical remarks heard by the audience but not other characters; also lead tracks on records.
